headline: Check Border Range and Military Access Information
reservation: Northumberland is England's least populated National Park with no general entry fee, though certain areas have specific restrictions. The Otterburn Training Area accounts for 23% of the park; some zones remain off-limits or require permission during live firing. Always check the official website for current military firing schedules and forest closure updates due to storm damage.

days.title: Roman Frontiers and Landscape Discovery

stops.name: The Sill: National Landscape Discovery Centre
stops.detail: Explore the park's gateway featuring an accessible Whin Sill Grassland roof walk with views of the Roman frontier.

stops.name: Sycamore Gap
stops.detail: Walk from Steel Rigg to witness one of the most iconic and photographed stretches of Hadrian’s Wall.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: The Sill is typically open 10 am to 4 pm.

days.title: Rugged Ridges and Dark Skies

stops.name: Simonside Hills
stops.detail: Trek the craggy profile of the ridge for 360-degree views of the Cheviots and the distant coastline.

stops.name: Cawfields
stops.detail: Visit this dramatic quarry site on Hadrian’s Wall which serves as an official Dark Sky Park viewing platform.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for winding moorland roads; conditions vary
days.note: Stargazing is best scheduled for the autumn and winter Dark Skies season.

days.title: The High Cheviots and Border Moorlands

stops.name: Linhope Spout
stops.detail: Hike to this dramatic waterfall tucked within the rolling grasslands and moors of the north.

stops.name: The Cheviot
stops.detail: Summit the highest point in Northumberland for an adventurous look across the Anglo-Scottish border.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for remote valley access; conditions vary
days.note: Much of this terrain is open moorland; check for local grazing restrictions.

intel.title: Military Range Zones
intel.text: The Otterburn Training Area covers nearly a quarter of the park and includes sites like the Otterburn Ranges. Access is strictly controlled; check official schedules as some parts are off-limits or require explicit permission.

intel.title: Dark Sky Season
intel.text: Official Dark Sky status makes this Europe's largest protected starry area, particularly at Walltown and Cawfields. Peak viewing begins in November as nights grow longer, though platforms are available year-round.

intel.title: Remote Services
intel.text: With only 2,000 residents across 410 square miles, services are concentrated in gateway towns like Rothbury or Wooler. Ensure supplies are secured before entering the predominantly uninhabited moorland core.

intel.title: Discovery Centre Access
intel.text: The Sill at Once Brewed is the primary hub for accessible parking and information. Seasonal sites like Walltown and Cawfields provide dedicated lots for hikers and stargazers.

intel.title: Far Horizon Connectivity
intel.text: Data and mobile signals are often unavailable in deep valleys like Coquetdale and the Harthope Valley. Download essential walking route updates or offline maps before leaving the main settlements.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Newcastle or Edinburgh and head to gateway towns like Hexham or Rothbury to stock up on supplies and check local trail status.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for most roads, though narrow passing lanes are common; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved moorland tracks.
plan.goldenHour: Simonside Hills offers panoramic sunset views, though cloud cover is frequent in this northern climate.
